&2010
Metropolia UAS led with 10% of total output
Health and welfare dominated with nearly one-third of all thesis production
Engineering and technology accounted for nearly one-quarter of output
Business and administration studies maintained a steady 20% sector share
Arts and culture output remained strong at 8.6% of total volume

&2011
Oulu UAS displaced Metropolia for the top position
Health and welfare share increased to 33% of total output
Engineering remained the second largest field of study
Arts and culture declined slightly from the previous year
Business and administrative sciences sustained steady production levels

&2012
Metropolia UAS reclaimed the position of highest thesis volume
Health and welfare sector reached a 33.7% share of production
Engineering and technology share experienced a slight decline to 23.8%
Business and administration reached 20.8% of total output
Education and humanities began showing consistent growth in absolute figures

&2013
Metropolia maintained its leading position among universities
Health and welfare output remained the largest subject area
Business and administration continued to grow in relative popularity
Arts and culture experienced a slight uptick in volume
Engineering output remained stable at 24% share

&2014
Metropolia remained the leading producer of academic theses
Health and welfare maintained a one-third share of all research
Business and administration reached a new high of 21.2%
Computer science began showing initial signs of increasing interest
Engineering sector output remained consistent across institutions

&2015
Metropolia solidified its top ranking with an 11.1% share
Health and welfare research reached 34.4% of total volume
Engineering represented roughly a quarter of all thesis output
Business and administration remained a critical pillar of study
Tourism and services maintained a steady 6.5% market share

&2016
Metropolia extended its lead to 11.7% of total research output
Health and wellbeing sectors consolidated as the primary field
Business and administration studies shifted toward a more unified classification
Engineering output showed a slight relative decline in sector share
Computing and information technology emerged as a distinct major category

&2017
Metropolia UAS reached 12.4% of total institutional output
Health and wellbeing research surged to 37.2% of all theses
Engineering output experienced a decrease in relative sector dominance
Computer science maintained a solid share of total research output
Education and teacher training began gaining more institutional focus

&2018
Metropolia maintained the top institutional position
Health and wellbeing continued to dominate with 36.7% share
Engineering and technology regained some momentum in research output
Computing and telecommunications grew to 7% of total volume
Arts and culture research stabilized below 5%

&2019
Metropolia remained the leader in total research volume
Health and welfare output slightly decreased but stayed dominant
Business and administration remained steady at 20.7%
Computing and telecommunications saw continued steady growth
Engineering remained the third largest field of study

&2020
Metropolia led with 11.3% of total thesis production
Business, administration, and law grew to 23.1% of output
Health and wellbeing remained the largest field despite a small dip
Computer science maintained a consistent 7.4% share
Engineering began to decline relative to other expanding fields

&2021
Metropolia UAS continued its long-term dominance in volume
Health and welfare saw a rebound to 35.8% of research
Business and legal studies remained very strong at 22.8%
Computing and IT continued its steady upward trajectory
Engineering share stabilized below 20% of total production

&2022
Metropolia retained the top rank among Finnish universities
Health and wellbeing remained the clear leader in subject distribution
Business, administration, and law sustained a 23% share
Computing continued to grow as a vital academic field
Engineering and technology maintained a stable 19% presence

&2023
Metropolia remained the largest institutional producer
Health and welfare reached 35.6% of total research output
Business and legal studies continued their strong growth trend
Computing and IT share increased to 8% of all theses
Engineering sector saw a relative decrease in its total share

&2024
Metropolia produced over 10% of total national thesis volume
Health and welfare output surged to over 11,000 units
Business and legal fields consolidated at nearly 23% share
Computing and IT grew significantly to 8.6% of total output
Engineering remained a core pillar with 18.5% of research

&2025
Metropolia UAS maintained its top position with 3,704 theses
Health and welfare reached a peak of 36% of all output
Computing and IT continued rapid growth, reaching 9.4% share
Business and administration remains the second largest academic sector
Engineering represents roughly 18% of the total research volume
